description: Cluster 1 is the biggest and most impactful cluster. It consists of 26 documents and has a total of 934 citations. Studies in this cluster emphasized the importance and connection of sub-themes such as RBV, supply chain, and organizational agility, which they linked to big data and Industry 4.0. The most cited articles in this cluster are Bag et al. 2021 (277 citations); Benzidia et al. 2021 (110 citations); Chiarini 2021 (97 citations); Nisar et al. 2021 (79 citations); and Waqas et al. 2021 (57 citations). Some studies have shed light on the direct relationship between BDA and sustainable performance (Afifa and Nguyen  2022; Al Halbusi et  al.  2023; Anwar et  al.  2024; Benzidia et al. 2021; Le and Vu 2024), while others have focused on the indirect role of BDA in sustainable performance via mediating mechanisms such as strategic agility, green innovation, green supply chains and process integration (Alyahya et al. 2023; Mehmood et al. 2024; Rashid et al. 2025; Waqas et al. 2021). Zhu et al. (2022) scrutinized the mediating role of BDA capabilities in the relationship between sustainable supply chain management practices and organizational performance, and Bag et al. (2021) focused on the role of AI-based GSCM in green supply chain management strategy in emerging economies.

This cluster consists of 20 documents cited 405 times. Studies in this cluster highlight AI adoption and its implementation by organizations to gain sustainable performance. The most frequently cited articles in this cluster are Bibri et  al.  (2024), Baabdullah et al. (2021), Frank (2021), Sætra (2021), and Hughes et al. (2021), which have been cited 85, 64, 55, 55, and 39 times, respectively. One group of studies highlighted the role of AI adoption and implementation in climate change and environmental performance (Bibri et  al.  2024; Baabdullah et  al.  2021; Frank  2021; Koyamparambath et  al.  2022; Lin et  al.  2024; Hao and Demir 2024). Bibri et al. (2024) and Frank (2021) emphasized the organizational implementation of AI to predict sustainable practices. Meanwhile, Baabdullah et al. (2021) highlighted the antecedents and consequences of successful acceptance of AI practices by SMEs in Saudi Arabia.

This cluster contains 19 documents that have been cited 96 times in total. It is ranked third in total publications and fourth in citations. This cluster focuses on major topics such as digital transformation, innovation, and disclosure embedded in ESG performance. The most frequently cited articles in this cluster are S. Wang and Esperança  (2023) (75 citations), Luo et  al.  (2024) (seven citations), Ma et al. (2023) (five citations), Z. Chen, Sugiyama, et al. 2024 (three citations), and Tian et al. (2024) (two citations). For example, He (2024) and Luo et al. (2024) shed light on the integration of digital transformation, innovation, AI adoption, and ESG. Liu et al. (2024), M. Wang and Zhang (2024), and S. Wang and Esperança (2023) demonstrate that AI enhances the extent of digital transformation and innovation, which in turn leads to ESG performance.

This cluster comprises 8 documents cited 27 times in total. It is ranked fourth in total publications and sixth in citations. This cluster summarizes the dynamic abilities of firms to respond to external challenges, supply chain disruption, and sustainability. The most coupled articles are Kholaif et  al.  (2022) (20 citations), Kumar et  al.  (2023) (two citations), S. Wang and Zhang (2024) (2 citations), (Camilleri et al. 2024) (one citation), and Mohamed Riyath and Inun Jariya (2024) (one citation). Kholaif et al. (2022) focused on the connection between the BDA capabilities of manufacturing firms and renewable energy supply chain management during COVID-19. Kumar et al. (2023) discussed how the use of machine learning and AI automation in organizations contributes to firm performance through the integration of dynamic capability initiatives. Using dynamic capability theory, S. Wang and Zhang  (2024) described how generative AI can augment ESG performance by strengthening innovation and collaboration within digital supply chains.

This cluster contains seven documents cited a total of 89 times and is ranked sixth in total publications and fifth in citations. This cluster focuses on the nexus of industrial robotics, blockchain, fintech, and carbon emissions and climate change. The most frequently cited articles in this cluster are Luan et  al.  (2022) (70 citations), Kazachenok et  al.  (2023) (nine citations), Hu et al. (2023) (five citations), Yang et al. (2023) (three citations), and Tabassum et al. (2024) (one citation). Luan et al. (2022) highlighted how industrial robotics contributes to air pollution and climate change. Kazachenok et al. (2023) considered the humanization of FinTech in the AI era through the incorporation of blockchain into ESG finance. Hu et al. (2023) described how attitudes toward AI and emissions trading schemes contribute to climate entrepreneurship and environmental performance. Yang et al. (2023) focused on the effect of the adoption of industrial robots on environmental performance through both the scale and energy-saving effects. Doran et al. (2024) discussed the importance of leveraging AI technologies to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions in European markets. Overall, this cluster summarizes the importance of digital technologies (i.e., robotics, blockchain, and FinTech) in carbon emissions control.
